segments: The daily commuter who leaves the house with a laptop, a lunch box and a water bottle and refuses to carry three bags for it
The returning Cabaia owner on their second or third purchase, now watching closely for the quality to slip
The traveller who plans trips around not paying for a checked bag, and needs the bag itself to be the thing that makes that possible
gaps: No price or free-entry terms found - emails cannot name a price, a trial length or a risk reversal

guarantees: Les produits sont-ils garantis ? Les modèles de notre collaboration exclusive avec Constance Gennari sont des créations en édition limitée, pensées sur des coupes et des architectures entièrement inédites. S'agissant de modèles éphémères produits en très petite série, nous ne disposerons pas de pièces de rechange ni de réassort sur le long terme pour assurer des réparations au-delà de cette période. C’est pourquoi ces pièces bénéficient d’une garantie de 2 ans, afin de vous assurer un accompagnement dédié durant leurs premières années sur le terrain. Nous apportons à ces modèles la même exigence de confection et de durabilité qu'à l'ensemble de nos collections.; Limited-edition, small production run; This explains why the 2-year warranty (rather than CABAIA's standard lifetime warranty cited elsewhere on the same page) applies to this specific limited run.

entries.verbatim: Quels produits composent la collection Léonard ? entries.claim: CABAIA Studio's first creative collaboration was entrusted to Constance Gennari, founder of The Socialite Family.
entries.verbatim: En quoi consiste la collaboration entre CABAIA Studio et Constance Gennari ? Quand l'esthétique affirmée de Constance Gennari rencontre la vision de CABAIA Studio, notre vestiaire prend une toute autre allure. C'est à la fondatrice de The Socialite Family que la marque confie les clés de son tout premier laboratoire créatif : une parenthèse stylistique inédite qui emprunte aux codes du design d'intérieur pour porter un nouveau regard sur nos pièces iconiques. La ligne CABAIA Studio revisite ainsi nos essentiels à travers des matières soigneusement choisies, des coupes inédites et un sens aigu du détail, pour une élégance naturelle qui vous laisse traverser les journées intenses sans perdre votre élan.

entries.claim: Because the Constance Gennari collaboration pieces are limited-edition models in entirely new cuts and architectures produced in very small runs, CABAIA will not have spare parts or restocking long-term to support repairs beyond the warranty period.
entries.verbatim: Les produits sont-ils garantis ? Les modèles de notre collaboration exclusive avec Constance Gennari sont des créations en édition limitée, pensées sur des coupes et des architectures entièrement inédites. S'agissant de modèles éphémères produits en très petite série, nous ne disposerons pas de pièces de rechange ni de réassort sur le long terme pour assurer des réparations au-delà de cette période. C’est pourquoi ces pièces bénéficient d’une garantie de 2 ans, afin de vous assurer un accompagnement dédié durant leurs premières années sur le terrain. Nous apportons à ces modèles la même exigence de confection et de durabilité qu'à l'ensemble de nos collections.

segments.name: The daily commuter who leaves the house with a laptop, a lunch box and a water bottle and refuses to carry three bags for it
segments.situation: Their bag is a working object, not an accessory: it goes to the office or into a vehicle every day and then straight on to a weekend without being unpacked. The same bag has to swallow a 13-15" laptop, papers, keys, a bottle and a packed meal, and it gets set down on floors, in car boots and on station platforms. They have already noticed what fails first — the base sags when it is full, the laptop sleeve is thin, the handles dig in once the bag is loaded, and a lunch bag that is one centimetre too short makes a bottle lie flat and leak. Several of them carry a lunch because the work pattern leaves no canteen: one reviewer describes using it as a bus driver, another used it through a weekend sports championship in heat up to 40°C.

objections.objection: It costs too much for a bag. 100€ for a work tote, 200€ for a suitcase, 45€ for a lunch bag — the equivalent is half that elsewhere and I only use it to carry things.
objections.answer: Buyers who say it is expensive say it in the same breath as saying it is worth it ('un peu cher mais très pratique en voyage', 'prix un peu élevé mais de très bonne qualité'). The concrete price answers are: the lifetime warranty with real part replacement — a broken wheel or trolley gets a new part from customer service (E384, E58) — free shipping over 50€, which almost every single product clears (E13), free returns within 14 days so the risk of being wrong is zero (E12), and interest-free instalments at checkout via Scalapay (E74, E249). Price is also anchored by the range: 30€ toiletry bag, 35€ bottle holder, 45€ lunch bag, 60€ cabas, 100€ carry-all, 200€ large case (E203, E86, E117, E41, E154, E45).

objections.objection: The build has been cheapened. The fabric is thinner than the older models, the base and sides are floppy, the laptop slot has no real padding and the handles are undersized — so the durability story is exactly where it is failing.
objections.answer: Nothing in the evidence answers this. The complaints are from named buyers on Cabaia's own product pages — material 'bien trop légère par rapport aux anciens modèles', 'côtés et surtout le fond du sac' not rigid enough, 'Manque de rembourrage', handles 'un peu mince pour l'importance du sac', a request for a reinforced outer base or corner studs. The only counterweights available are an unattributed in-house load test on the suitcases (handles to 110kg, straps and telescopic handle to 130kg — no testing body named, E66), an undated vendor claim that a suitcase survived extreme testing (E386), the toiletry bag's 'ultra-resistant' fabric claim (E212), and other buyers saying the products are 'jolis, solides et bien conçus' (E326). There is no documented failure rate, no third-party durability certification, and no stated change-of-materials explanation. Do not write durability claims against this objection — write the warranty and the free return instead.

objections.objection: 'Guaranteed for life' is marketing language. Nobody honours that, and I will be told my case was misused.
objections.answer: Partly answered, and the honest version is stronger than the slogan. The only concrete mechanism in the evidence is for suitcases: if a wheel or the trolley breaks, customer service sends a replacement part under the lifetime warranty (E384). Cabaia states the lifetime guarantee for accessories generally (E101, E58, E163) and one buyer reports a defective bag exchanged quickly via the Annecy boutique (E306) — one customer's experience, not a policy. Against it, the same site contradicts itself: the CABAIA Studio collaboration pieces are guaranteed two years, explicitly because they are small-run with no long-term spare parts (E234, E247), while a spec block on the same page still says 'Garantie à vie' (E248). There is no published claims process, time limit, wear-and-tear exclusion list or claim approval rate anywhere in the evidence. Write the wheel-replacement promise, not the word 'lifetime' on its own.

objections.objection: I cannot judge a bag from photos — the real size, the stiffness, how it sits loaded — and the size charts are a maze of named cities and litres.
objections.answer: Returns are free within 14 days, which makes buying the wrong size reversible at no cost (E12, E303), and delivery is free from 50€ (E13) with 3 business days to a pickup point or standard address after a 4–5 day dispatch (E15, E11). The product pages publish exact external dimensions, volume, weight and a carry-on yes/no for each size, plus side-by-side comparison tables against other models (E5, E3, E4, E43, E78, E80, E291, E113, E260–E267, E72). There are eight boutiques — Paris, Marseille, Namur, Caen, Montpellier, Rouen, Grenoble, Dusseldorf — for anyone who wants to handle one first (E287). The gap: a buyer reports the shops do not carry enough of the range to do that ('pas assez de modèles en boutique', E153), and one lives far from any large store (E200).

objections.objection: The product page overstates what it does. It advertises a phone pocket that will not take a phone — if that claim is wrong, what else is?
objections.answer: The specification does carry a real limit, and it should be quoted instead of the marketing line: the bottle holder's dedicated pocket takes a phone up to 165x80x25mm (E346) — which is smaller than many current handsets, and that is why buyers say 'la poche de devant, trop petite pour y ranger son mobile' and 'un peu juste pour tous les modèles de portables'. One buyer goes further and says the Cabaia AI assistant told them it would take a phone and it does not (E114). Free returns within 14 days cover the mistake (E106). There is nothing in the evidence that defends the unqualified 'poche téléphone intégrée' claim (E93) against these reports — stop making it and state the millimetres.

objections.objection: If I order it, it may not turn up, or the one I want will be out of stock — and buying it in a shop means losing the online offer.
objections.answer: Barely answered. Cabaia publishes dispatch in 4–5 business days and 3 business days to a pickup point or home in France métropolitaine, free from 50€ (E11, E14, E15, E13), 15–20€ and 8 days to DOM TOM (E17), free returns in 14 days (E12), and customer service Monday to Friday 10h–17h30 (E304). None of that covers the three things buyers actually report: a carrier losing the parcel entirely, an order still not received weeks later, and a bag permanently out of stock online while the boutique refuses the online promotion. There is no stated lost-parcel policy, no restock commitment, and no price-parity policy between web and shops in the evidence.

objections.objection: I will buy it as a cabin bag and still be charged at the gate — the airline lists on the page contradict each other.
objections.answer: The evidence answers this only by admitting it. For the duffle, the page lists Emirates, IndiGo and Singapore Airlines as free in cabin and names Air France, KLM, British Airways, Iberia, American Airlines and Delta as possibly charging extra (E19, E20), while a separate spec block lists Air France, KLM, Lufthansa and SWISS as compatible with no caveat (E18). For the Carry All at 37 x 27 x 16 cm the claim is 'accepté sans supplément' on a named list including Air France, Ryanair, Lufthansa, EasyJet, KLM, Transavia and Delta (E195, E315), with the instruction to check your own airline because the allowance varies by ticket type. The soft cases are clearer and more honest: Small is free on Air France KLM, British Airways, Iberia, Indigo, Swiss and Lufthansa, costs a supplement on Transavia and EasyJet, and medium and large must be checked (E381, E382, E383). Write the dimensions and the per-airline caveat, never a blanket 'cabin approved'.

objections.objection: I already own a bag that works. Nothing here is a reason to buy another one this month.
objections.answer: The only honest lever in the evidence is that one Cabaia piece replaces several: the Carry All is 16L for a full workday or an improvised weekend, carried three ways — hand, shoulder with the integrated handles, or crossbody (E310, E312, E166) — with a 15" laptop pocket, a bottle pocket, a zipped back pocket, a key carabiner and a luggage pass-through (E159, E168, E169, E170, E171), and buyers confirm they use the same bag for work and weekends (E327, E328). The duffle changes face with two interchangeable MOLLE pouches and converts between hand, shoulder, crossbody and backpack (E37, E34, E26, E29). One buyer bought three nesting suitcase sizes; another owns the backpack, the cabin case and the 110L (E375, E378). That is an argument for consolidation, not an urgent trigger — there is no deadline, no promotion and no stock scarcity in the evidence to create one, and the 'limited edition' CABAIA Studio line carries no dates or quantities (E70, E145).

objections.objection: The eco positioning is greenwashing. Recycled polyester made in a Cambodian factory is still a plastic bag with a label on it.
objections.answer: This one is actually well evidenced. B Corp certified since 2022 and an entreprise à mission since 2021 (E282, E281, E216); materials labelled GRS, EVE VEGAN and GOTS (E8, E142, E235); external production workshops certified BSCI or SMETA for ethical, social and environmental compliance (E9, E217); 68.6% of products contain recycled plastic (E283); 424,057€ paid to partner associations (E284); per-product composition published, e.g. 100% recycled polyester outer on the duffle and lunch bag, 70% recycled cotton / 30% recycled polyester on the Carry All (E6, E122, E160); vegan and water-repellent across the range (E35, E83, E165). The weak spots to avoid: a bare 'Ateliers certifiés' claim with no certifying body named (E84), and a buyer noting the toiletry bag is made in Cambodia (E268) — the certifications cover audit standards, not local manufacture location, and nothing in the evidence states where each product is made.

objections.objection: The designer piece I actually want is a limited run with only two years of cover and no spare parts afterwards — that is the opposite of buying something to keep.
objections.answer: Cabaia states this itself rather than hiding it: the Constance Gennari pieces are limited-edition creations on entirely new cuts, produced in very small series, so there will be no spare parts or restocking long-term to support repairs beyond the period — which is why they carry a 2-year guarantee, with the same making and durability standards as the rest of the collections (E247, E234). The Léonard line is three coordinated pieces — backpack, handbag and pouch that clips inside by day and is worn alone at night — each in three vegan materials, at 99€ for the handbag (E245, E226). What is not answered: nothing resolves the contradiction with the 'Garantie à vie' line printed on the same page (E248), and there is no quantity, no end date and no repair path after year two. For a buyer whose whole reason to pay this much is longevity, this objection stands.
